Ryugo

bibl.title: Tonotopic Organization of Vertical Cells in the Dorsal Cochlear Nucleus of the CBA/J Mouse

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the spatial arrangement of vertical cells in the dorsal cochlear nucleus with respect to frequency
span.quote: To address this issue, we retrogradely labeled vertical cells via physiologically targeted injections in the AVCN of the CBA/J mouse. Results from multiple cases were merged with a normalized 3D template of the cochlear nucleus ( Muniak et al., 2013 ) to quantitatively demonstrate that the arrangement of vertical cells is tonotopic and aligned to the innervation pattern of the AN.

span.label: whether vertical cells and their projections are tonotopically organised in the intact mammalian brain, which had been inferred but never directly shown
span.quote: Differing lines of physiological and anatomical evidence suggest that vertical cells and their projections are organized with respect to frequency, but this has not been conclusively demonstrated in the intact mammalian brain.

span.label: converts an inference drawn from indirect evidence into a direct quantitative demonstration in 3D, and shows the arrangement is aligned to auditory nerve innervation
span.quote: Collectively, these indirect lines of evidence imply that vertical cells of the DCN are tonotopically organized. There is, however, scant direct evidence to support this conclusion in the intact mammalian brain

span.label: existence
span.quote: Various quantitative approaches converged to the same conclusion that vertical cells are tonotopically organized within the DCN.

span.label: tonotopic organisation of dorsal cochlear nucleus vertical cells
span.quote: Our results demonstrate that vertical cells are arranged tonotopically and send projections to matched frequency regions of the AVCN.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: Single- and multi-unit recordings were performed with glass micropipettes (1.2 mm outer diameter) containing fluorescein dextran-amine (MW10,000; D-1820; Molecular Probes/Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA) or tetramethylrhodamine dextran-amine (MW10,000; D-1817; Molecular Probes), each diluted to 10% w/v in a solution of 0.5M Tris buffer, pH 7.6, and 3M NaCl.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Auditory-nerve input pattern sets each cochlear nucleus neuron's best frequency, so the cochleotopic auditory-nerve projection imposes tonotopy on vertical cells
span.quote: Given evidence that the pattern of AN input largely determines the BF of neurons in the CN ( Bourk et al., 1981 ; Fekete et al., 1984 ; Spirou et al., 1993 ; Ryugo and May, 1993 ), it is reasonable to conclude that the arrangement of vertical cell BFs would follow suit.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Vertical cell axons ramify locally inside an isofrequency slab, which is what makes their inhibition of pyramidal (type IV) cells fall at or near best frequency
span.quote: Thus, the near-BF inhibition of type IV units (pyramidal cells) by type II units is a result of the local ramification of vertical cell axons within an isofrequency slab.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Frequency-specific inhibitory demand in the cochlear nucleus, set by the gains and spectral notches of the mouse ear transfer function, shapes how many vertical cells are found at each frequency
span.quote: Hence, the distribution of vertical cell numbers might relate to the overall inhibitory requirements in the CN with respect to frequency.

span.label: retrograde labelling from a physiologically characterised AVCN site gives every labelled DCN cell an inherited BF, since the injection site's BF is measured and the cell's is not
span.quote: Furthermore, comparisons to a frequency model of the CN ( Muniak et al., 2013 ) demonstrated that the BF of each cell, inferred from the AVCN recording site, closely matched that of AN input.

span.label: normalising every case into one 3D template lets cells from separate animals be merged into a single dataset
span.quote: Cases were normalized by independently aligning each surface to a template CN surface ( Muniak et al., 2013 ) using an iterative routine in Amira that produced an affine transformation matrix.

span.label: dendrites and local axons stay within an isofrequency sheet defined by the incoming auditory nerve fibres, so inhibition lands on matched frequencies
span.quote: For each cell, the collective dendritic arborization formed a “spatial envelope” that conformed to an isofrequency sheet defined by the incoming auditory nerve fibers.

span.label: a disynaptic tuberculoventral pathway whose delay is set by conduction velocity plus one synapse, proposed for echo suppression
span.quote: It has been proposed that this connection may be a disynaptic pathway for echo suppression ( Wickesberg and Oertel, 1990 ; Wickesberg, 1996 ), with the timing of the inhibitory projection to the AVCN offset by the axon conduction velocity and a single synaptic delay.

span.label: near-BF inhibition of type IV units follows from vertical cell axons ramifying inside a single isofrequency slab
span.quote: The tonotopic distribution of vertical cells demonstrated in the present study fits well with this picture, and the 3D grouping of cells associated with the same BF affirms the idea that cell types united by a common frequency in the DCN are organized into slabs

span.label: glycinergic inhibition sharpens spike timing in bushy and T-stellate cells on different timescales
span.quote: Because many natural sounds, including communication signals, are characterized by distinct, time-varying changes in their spectral peaks, the type II – type IV circuitry could facilitate the detection of spectral features embedded within these sounds

span.label: BF confirmed by an automated 4-octave sweep at 20 dB above threshold, sampled every 1/25 octave
span.quote: BF and threshold were estimated audiovisually and then confirmed using an automated tuning curve protocol that measured responses to a 4-octave (oct.) frequency sweep centered on the test frequency at 20 dB above threshold, sampling every 1/25-oct.

span.label: Retrograde filling was incomplete, so cells could only be characterised from the soma and primary dendrites rather than the full dendritic arbor.
span.note: what this limits: every morphological characterisation: OUR RETROGRADE FILLS WERE INSUFFICIENT TO REVEAL THE FULL DENDRITIC ARBORIZATION OF EACH NEURON, SO MORPHOLOGICAL CHARACTERIZATIONS HAD TO BE BASED PRIMARILY UPON THE SOMA AND PRIMARY PROCESSES
span.quote: Our retrograde fills were insufficient to reveal the full dendritic arborization of each neuron, so morphological characterizations had to be based primarily upon the soma and primary processes.

span.label: Injection size, a possible confound for the cell counts, could not be measured reliably.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison of cell counts across injections: QUANTIFYING THE SIZE OF AN INJECTION SITE IS NOTORIOUSLY DIFFICULT DUE TO THE AMBIGUITY IN DETERMINING THE EDGE OF THE EFFECTIVE UPTAKE REGION
span.quote: Quantifying the size of an injection site is notoriously difficult due to the ambiguity in determining the edge of the effective uptake region.

span.label: The functional role of vertical cells is not settled by these anatomical results and needs further data.
span.note: what this limits: any functional claim about vertical cells: MORE DATA ARE NEEDED TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE FUNCTION OF THESE NEURONS
span.quote: Overall, these results suggest that vertical cells provide rapid on- or near-BF inhibition both to cells of the DCN and AVCN, although more data are needed to better understand the function of these neurons.

span.label: the size of an injection site cannot be quantified because the edge of the effective uptake region is ambiguous
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1 - injection size is not reliably quantifiable
span.quote: Quantifying the size of an injection site is notoriously difficult due to the ambiguity in determining the edge of the effective uptake region.

span.label: apparent injection size is further distorted by photobleaching and exposure time
span.note: what this limits: the apparent injection size specifically: THE APPARENT SIZE OF A FLUORESCENT INJECTION SITE IS SUBJECT TO THE EFFECTS OF PHOTOBLEACHING AND EXPOSURE TIME WHEN COLLECTING IMAGES
span.quote: Furthermore, the apparent size of a fluorescent injection site is subject to the effects of photobleaching and exposure time when collecting images.

span.label: retrograde fills were incomplete, so morphology had to be judged from soma and primary processes alone
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[0] · what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - soma and primary processes only
span.quote: Our retrograde fills were insufficient to reveal the full dendritic arborization of each neuron, so morphological characterizations had to be based primarily upon the soma and primary processes.

span.label: some cells labelled at the wrong end of the frequency axis are attributed to axons of passage, an artifact of the tracer method
span.note: what this limits: the low-frequency cells found after high-BF injections: THIS RESULT IS LIKELY DUE TO THE LABELING OF AXONS OF PASSAGE
span.quote: We did note that high-BF injections tended to produce slightly greater numbers of cells in lower frequency regions within the model. This result, however, is likely due to the labeling of axons of passage: the trajectory of low-BF vertical cell axons passes through high frequency regions in the AVCN

span.label: the excess of low-BF cells is left explicitly unexplained rather than resolved
span.note: what this limits: the low-BF labelling asymmetry, quantified and left open: LOW BF INJECTIONS TENDED TO LABEL MORE VERTICAL CELLS THAN HIGH BF INJECTIONS (R2 = 0.32, P < 0.003), THOUGH THE REASON FOR THIS TONOTOPIC FEATURE IS UNCLEAR
span.quote: Low BF injections tended to label more vertical cells than high BF injections ( Fig. 5B ; R 2 = 0.32, P < 0.003), though the reason for this tonotopic feature is unclear.

span.label: the function of these neurons is still open; the anatomy does not settle it
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[2] · what this limits: the same scope as item 2 - the anatomy does not settle the function
span.quote: Overall, these results suggest that vertical cells provide rapid on- or near-BF inhibition both to cells of the DCN and AVCN, although more data are needed to better understand the function of these neurons.

span.label: 21 mice, 19 of them female, with no analysis by sex
span.note: what this limits: any sex-general reading of the results: TWENTY-ONE ADULT CBA/J MICE (2 MALE, 19 FEMALE), with no analysis by sex
span.quote: Twenty-one adult CBA/J mice (2 male, 19 female; Jackson Laboratories, Bar Harbor, ME) were used in this study.

span.label: image levels and colour were adjusted per case, defended on the ground that the analysis used position and not luminance
span.note: what this limits: the image-based measurements: LEVEL ADJUSTMENTS AND COLOR ENHANCEMENTS WERE APPLIED TO BRING OUT WEAK SIGNALS, defended because OUR ANALYSIS FOCUSED ON THE LOCATION OF LABELED PIXELS rather than their intensity
span.quote: In some cases, level adjustments and color enhancements were applied to bring out weak signals and to balance the overall amount of background signal across channels. Because our analysis focused on the location of labeled pixels but not pixel luminance, these manipulations did not alter our findings.

span.label: a frequency model built from AN innervation by cochlear origin, imported as an external criterion against which cell positions are predicted
span.quote: This model is based on the distribution of AN innervation in the CN with respect to cochlear origin, and makes no assumptions about nor imposes directionality to frequency organization throughout the volume of the nucleus.

span.label: the pinna transfer function and the frequency range of spectral notches, used to explain an anatomical cell-count gradient
span.quote: With the mouse ear, spectral notches are largely observed in the >20 kHz range ( Lauer et al., 2011 ), which is where our vertical cell counts are the lowest. Furthermore, the transfer function of the mouse ear shows overall gains in the 10 – 20 kHz range ( Lauer et al., 2011 ), where our cell counts are higher.

span.label: the tonotopic finding corroborated by independently constructing a three-dimensional surface of the deep layer
span.note: eliminates: a pattern that exists only in the projection or sectioning used to find it - the 3D reconstruction is built from the same tissue by a different route
span.quote: We corroborated this finding by creating a 3D surface of the deep layer ( Fig.

span.label: type II electrophysiological response
span.quote: Vertical cells are the presumed source of the type II electrophysiological response in the DCN, characterized as having a “V”-shaped excitatory area flanked by inhibitory sidebands, low rates of spontaneous activity, nonmonotonic rate-level functions, poor responses to broadband noise stimuli, and robust responses to tones near their best frequency (BF; Evans and Nelson, 1973 ; Young and Brownell, 1976 ; Young and Voigt, 1982 ; Davis et al., 1996 ; Spirou et al., 1999 ; Rhode, 1999 ).

span.label: tonotopic and cochleotopic are used here as TWO DIFFERENT organisations that are compared - the arrangement of cell BFs versus the arrangement of auditory nerve input by cochlear origin; their alignment is the paper's result, so the terms cannot be synonyms in this paper
span.quote: In addition, comparisons are made to a quantitative model of frequency representation in the cochlear nucleus (CN; Muniak et al., 2013 ) to show that this tonotopic arrangement is well aligned to the cochleotopic organization of the DCN.

span.label: BF, for a vertical cell, is not measured at that cell; it is inherited from the physiologically characterised AVCN injection site that labelled it
span.quote: Furthermore, comparisons to a frequency model of the CN ( Muniak et al., 2013 ) demonstrated that the BF of each cell, inferred from the AVCN recording site, closely matched that of AN input.

span.label: type II names a response category, used throughout as a proxy for a cell class on the strength of a presumed identification
span.quote: Vertical cells are the presumed source of the type II electrophysiological response in the DCN, characterized as having a “V”-shaped excitatory area flanked by inhibitory sidebands, low rates of spontaneous activity, nonmonotonic rate-level functions, poor responses to broadband noise stimuli, and robust responses to tones near their best frequency

span.label: tonotopic organization —operationalised-as→ principal component analysis
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — one of four independent operationalisations of the same claim in this paper
span.quote: We used various methods to quantitatively evaluate the tonotopic organization of vertical cells. First, we performed principal component analysis on the normalized dataset, and visualized the axis of the first principal component in three (spatial) dimensions, allowing it to pass through the Euclidian center of mass of the dataset ( Fig. 5A , black line). Not surprisingly, this axis was oriented towards the postero-dorsomedial corner of the DCN. The first principal component accounted for 75% of the variance in the dataset ( Fig. 5D ), indicating vertical cells are largely organized along one dimension in the DCN with respect to frequency.

span.label: tonotopic organization —operationalised-as→ multiple regression analysis

span.label: R = 0.34, P = 0.092 — cochlear labelling spread against cell counts, offered as evidence that injection size did not drive the counts
span.quote: Another approach to the question that did not require injection quantification was to compare cell counts to other neural elements labeled by the injections, such as AN fibers that can be traced back to their cochlear origins ( Muniak et al., 2013 ). If injection size co-varies with tracer uptake, then one might expect a larger injection to produce both larger cell counts and broader labeling in the cochlea. There was a poor relationship, however, between these parameters ( R = 0.34, P = 0.092; see “Spread %” in Table 2 from Muniak et al., 2013 ), suggesting our counts were not significantly skewed by variations in injection size.
